description: Incremental Phase 2 evidence for the 0.7.0 T2/T3 backfill. Passing backfill evidence does not add a component to the package manifest's certifiedComponents list until the 0.7.0 release gate is complete.

limitations: Phase 2 browser automation currently covers the canonical Bootstrap 5.3.3 lane in Chromium; the complete 0.7.0 gate will rerun the supported Bootstrap and browser matrices.

The fixture proves explicit opt-in initialization, keyboard-focus show/focusout dismissal, aria-describedby ownership, viewport-edge placement flipping, repeated use, hidden-state disposal and reinitialization, no backdrop or scroll lock, accessibility, responsive/RTL rendering, and clean console/page-error evidence.
Bootstrap Tooltip does not own an Escape-key listener; its applicable keyboard dismissal contract is focusout. Tooltip does not create a backdrop or scroll lock.
The normalized screenshot is a render smoke and has no accepted regression baseline yet.
Real-device and generic host-conformance evidence remain pending.

resolvedFindings: Listbox option wrappers and grouped lists use presentation roles so axe recognizes the required option ownership chain.
The public ESM module owns Combobox behavior and lifecycle while the catalog imports the same module instead of carrying a private duplicate.

Phase 2 records Alert Dialog as a Tier 3 confirmation composition of Dialog, Button, and the Bootstrap Modal static-backdrop contract; the complete 0.7.0 gate will rerun the supported Bootstrap and browser matrices.

The fixture proves static backdrop and disabled Escape dismissal, Bootstrap hidePrevented feedback, title/description wiring, no header close button, action-button dismissal, focus traversal, focus return, repeated use, responsive/RTL/theme rendering, accessibility, and clean console/page-error evidence.

Alert Dialog owns no separate JavaScript implementation: Bootstrap Modal owns the backdrop, focus trap, scroll lock, and lifecycle while the Alert Dialog macro fixes the confirmation-only structure and static options.
No empty, loading, or async error state applies to this synchronous confirmation primitive; longer workflows should compose Dialog with application-specific content.

Phase 2 records Menubar as a Tier 3 composition of the already-certified Dropdown Menu, Checkbox, Radio Group, and Button primitives; the complete 0.7.0 gate will rerun the supported Bootstrap and browser matrices.

The fixture proves the accepted role=group container contract, absence of unsupported ARIA menubar/menuitem semantics, independent Bootstrap dropdown keyboard and Escape behavior, sibling menu closing, auto_close="outside" for form controls inside menus, Dropdown instance lifecycle availability, responsive/RTL/theme rendering, accessibility, and clean console/page-error evidence.

Bootstrap does not ship a shadcn-style roving menubar or nested submenu primitive. Moo UI intentionally documents submenu as an unsupported gap instead of spoofing roles or hover/roving behavior it cannot back.
Menubar owns no separate JavaScript implementation: Bootstrap Dropdown owns trigger state, menu positioning, keyboard handling, dismissal, and lifecycle for each grouped menu.
